AL.registrationDeadlineNote: Last day to register to vote for the November 3, 2026 general election is Monday, October 19, 2026 (15 days before the election).
AL.earlyVotingNote: Alabama has no early in-person voting. Voters who qualify may vote absentee in person at the county absentee election manager's office before Election Day.
AL.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. Only voters who meet one of the reasons listed on the absentee ballot application (for example, physical illness or infirmity) may vote absentee. A copy of your photo ID must be included with the application.
AL.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, mailed ballots received by noon; hand delivered ballots by close of business November 2, 2026
AL.idRequirement: Alabama requires a photo ID to vote at the polls. Acceptable IDs include an Alabama driver's license or non-driver ID, Alabama photo voter ID card, U.S. passport, government or Alabama college employee or student ID, military ID, or tribal ID. Without ID you may vote a provisional ballot and show ID by 5 p.m. the Friday after the election, or vote a regular ballot if two election officials positively identify you.

AK.registrationDeadlineNote: Registration or updates must be postmarked or received 30 days before the election. Division of Elections offices are open October 3 and October 4, 2026 for registration.
AK.earlyVotingNote: Early and absentee in-person voting begins October 19, 2026 and runs through Election Day at designated locations. Regional offices are also open some weekend hours.
AK.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed. Alaska is a no-excuse absentee state.
AK.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received by November 13, 2026 (November 18, 2026 if mailed from overseas)
AK.idRequirement: You must be prepared to show one form of identification at the polls, such as a voter ID card, driver's license, state ID, passport, military ID, birth certificate, or hunting or fishing license. A current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, government check, or other government document with your name and address also works. Absentee by-mail ballots require one identifier and a witness signature on the return envelope.

AZ.registrationDeadlineNote: Register by 11:59 p.m. on October 5, 2026, online, by mail, or in person.
AZ.earlyVotingNote: Early voting begins October 7, 2026. In-person early voting runs until the Friday before Election Day; October 30, 2026 is computed from that stated rule. Check your county recorder for locations and hours.
AZ.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed. Voters can join the Active Early Voting List or make a one-time request through their county recorder.
AZ.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by 7:00 p.m. at the county recorder, a drop box, or any voting location in your county
AZ.idRequirement: Every voter must show proof of identity at the polls. Bring one photo ID with your name and address (such as an Arizona driver license), or two documents without a photo that show your name and address (such as a utility bill and bank statement), or one photo ID without an address plus one document with your address.

AR.registrationDeadlineNote: The 30-day deadline falls on Sunday, October 4, 2026, so it advances to the next business day, Monday, October 5, 2026, under the state election calendar.
AR.earlyVotingNote: Early voting runs 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Friday and 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Saturday, ending at 5 p.m. on Monday, November 2, 2026.
AR.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. You may vote absentee if you will be unavoidably absent from your polling site on Election Day, unable to attend due to illness or physical disability, in the uniformed services or merchant marine (or a spouse or dependent) away from home, or living temporarily outside the United States.
AR.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, mailed ballots received by 7:30 p.m.; ballots delivered in person by close of business October 30, 2026
AR.idRequirement: Voters are asked to show an approved form of ID at the polls, such as a driver's license, photo ID card, concealed handgun carry license, U.S. passport, military ID, or a state college employee badge or student ID. Without ID you may cast a provisional ballot and either sign a sworn statement or show ID to the county clerk by noon the Monday after the election.

CA.registrationDeadlineNote: After October 19, 2026 you can still register conditionally and vote in person through Election Day.
CA.earlyVotingNote: Early voting sites open October 5, 2026 and vote-by-mail ballots go out by that date. Vote centers in Voter's Choice Act counties open October 24, 2026. Ballot drop boxes are available October 6 through November 3, 2026.
CA.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Every registered voter is mailed a ballot automatically. No request is needed. October 27, 2026 is the last day to ask by mail for a replacement or a ballot sent to a different address.
CA.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received by November 10, 2026
CA.idRequirement: In most cases you do not need to show ID to vote in California. If you are voting for the first time after registering by mail and did not give a driver license, state ID number, or last four digits of your Social Security number, you may be asked for ID such as a driver's license, passport, student ID, or utility bill.

CO.registrationDeadlineNote: October 26, 2026 is the last day to register online, by mail, or at an agency and still get a ballot in the mail. You can register in person at a voter service and polling center through Election Day.
CO.earlyVotingNote: Voter service and polling centers must be open by October 19, 2026 and stay open through Election Day. Drop boxes accept ballots starting October 12, 2026.
CO.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Every active registered voter is mailed a ballot automatically. County clerks must send ballots by October 9, 2026.
CO.idRequirement: Voters who vote in person must show ID. Acceptable IDs include a Colorado driver's license or ID card, U.S. passport, military ID, Colorado student ID with photo, or a recent utility bill, bank statement, or government document with your name and address. First-time mail voters may need to include a copy of ID with their ballot.

CT.registrationDeadlineNote: Mailed registrations must arrive and online registrations must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. on October 16, 2026. After that, you can use same-day registration during early voting and on Election Day.
CT.earlyVotingNote: Early voting runs October 19 through November 1, 2026 at your town's early voting location.
CT.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed. Public Act 26-42 removed the excuse requirement for absentee ballots.
CT.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the town clerk by close of polls at 8:00 p.m.
CT.idRequirement: Poll workers ask for ID, but photo ID is not required. You can show a Social Security card or any pre-printed ID with your name and address, name and signature, or name and photo. If you have no ID, in most cases you can sign an affidavit instead. Some first-time voters who registered by mail must show ID or vote provisionally.

DE.registrationDeadlineNote: Registration closes Saturday, October 10, 2026. Military and overseas voters have until October 19, 2026.
DE.earlyVotingNote: Early voting runs October 22 through November 1, 2026 with no early voting on Sunday, October 25. Hours are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. October 22 to 24 and October 26 to 27, and 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. October 28 to November 1.
DE.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. You may vote absentee if you are in public service or away from the country, unable to vote due to your business or occupation (including students, caregivers, and incarcerated persons), sick or physically disabled, on vacation, or unable to vote because of your religion.
DE.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the county elections office by close of polls at 8:00 p.m.
DE.idRequirement: You will be asked to show identification at the polls, but Delaware has no photo ID law. If your name is on the poll list and you have no ID, you may sign an affidavit affirming your identity.

DC.registrationDeadlineNote: October 13, 2026 is the deadline for mailed and online registrations. You can also register in person during early voting and on Election Day.
DC.earlyVotingNote: Early Vote Centers are open every day October 26 through November 1, 2026, 8:30 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.
DC.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Every registered voter is mailed a ballot automatically. Ballots are scheduled to begin going out around September 28, 2026.
DC.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received by November 13, 2026; drop box or Vote Center returns by 8:00 p.m. on November 3, 2026
DC.idRequirement: Registered voters do not need to show ID to vote. If you are voting in DC for the first time and did not provide proof of residence when you registered, you must show proof of residence, such as a DC DMV ID, utility bill, bank statement, or lease.

FL.registrationDeadlineNote: Book closing is 29 days before the election. Online, mail, and in-person registration must be done by October 5, 2026.
FL.earlyVotingNote: October 24 through October 31, 2026 is the mandatory statewide early voting period. Some counties may offer additional days; check your county Supervisor of Elections.
FL.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed. A voter, an immediate family member, a legal guardian, or a designee for a voter with a disability may make the request.
FL.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by 7:00 p.m. local time
FL.idRequirement: Bring a current and valid photo ID with a signature, such as a Florida driver license, Florida ID card, U.S. passport, military ID, or student ID. If your photo ID has no signature, bring a second ID with a signature. Without ID you can vote a provisional ballot that counts if your signature matches your registration record.
FL.officialSiteLabel: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections

GA.registrationDeadlineNote: Last day to register to vote for the November 3, 2026 general election.
GA.earlyVotingNote: Advance in-person voting runs October 13 through October 30, 2026, including two Saturdays. Hours and locations are set by each county.
GA.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed. Requests open August 17, 2026. You must provide an ID number or a copy of acceptable ID with the application.
GA.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the county before the polls close
GA.idRequirement: You must show a government-issued photo ID to vote in person. Accepted IDs include a Georgia driver license (even if expired), free state voter ID card, U.S. passport, military ID, public college student ID, or government employee ID.

HI.registrationDeadlineNote: Paper registration applications must reach your County Elections Division by October 26, 2026. You may also register online at any time or in person at a voter service center through Election Day.
HI.earlyVotingNote: Hawaii votes by mail. Voter service centers open October 20 through November 3, 2026 (excluding Sundays) for in-person voting, same day registration, and ballot drop off.
HI.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Every registered voter is mailed a ballot automatically. Ballots arrive by October 16, 2026. No request is needed.
HI.idRequirement: Hawaii mails ballots to all voters, and ballots are verified by signature. Extra proof of ID is required only if you are registering for the first time in Hawaii by mail and cannot provide a Hawaii driver license, state ID, or Social Security number.

ID.registrationDeadlineNote: Pre-registration must be received by the county clerk by 5 p.m. on October 23, 2026. After that, you can register in person during early voting or at your polling place on Election Day with photo ID and proof of residence.
ID.earlyVotingNote: Early voting is a county option. Where offered it may begin October 13, 2026 and ends at 5 p.m. on October 30, 2026. Check with your county clerk.
ID.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
ID.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the county clerk by 8:00 p.m.
ID.idRequirement: Be prepared to show a photo ID: an Idaho driver license or ID card, U.S. passport or federal photo ID, tribal ID, or an Idaho concealed weapons license. The state FAQ also describes signing a Personal Identification Affidavit if you have no photo ID; confirm with your county clerk.

IN.registrationDeadlineNote: Registration closes 29 days before the election. Online applications are accepted until midnight on October 5, 2026.
IN.earlyVotingNote: In-person absentee (early) voting at the county clerk's office or satellite sites runs October 6, 2026 through noon on November 2, 2026.
IN.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. Reasons include being absent from the county all 12 hours the polls are open, working the whole time polls are open, being age 65 or older, disability, illness or confinement, caring for a confined person, election duties, lack of transportation, religious observance, and certain other categories.
IN.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by 6:00 p.m. local time
IN.idRequirement: You must show a photo ID issued by Indiana or the U.S. government that shows your name (matching your registration), your photo, and an expiration date that is current or expired after November 5, 2024. Without ID you may cast a provisional ballot and have until noon 10 days after the election to show ID or claim an exemption.
IN.officialSiteLabel: Indiana Secretary of State, Election Division

IA.registrationDeadlineNote: Pre-registration deadline is October 19, 2026 (15 days before the election). You can also register on Election Day at your polling place with proof of identity and residence.
IA.earlyVotingNote: In-person absentee voting at the county auditor's office runs October 14 through November 2, 2026.
IA.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed. Written request must reach the county auditor.
IA.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the county auditor before 8:00 p.m.
IA.idRequirement: You must show one acceptable ID: Iowa driver license or non-operator ID, Iowa voter ID card, U.S. passport, U.S. military or veteran ID, or tribal ID. If you have no ID, another registered voter in your precinct may attest to your identity, or you may use Election Day registration documents.

KS.registrationDeadlineNote: Deadline to register or update your name or address for the 2026 general election is October 13, 2026 (21 days before the election).
KS.earlyVotingNote: Advance in-person voting may begin as early as October 14, 2026 and must begin in all counties by October 27, 2026. Check your county election office for hours and the last day to vote in person.
KS.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed. The application must include your driver license number or a copy of your photo ID.
KS.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by close of polls
KS.idRequirement: You must show photo ID to vote in person, such as a driver license or ID card from any state, U.S. passport, military ID, tribal ID, government employee badge, Kansas college student ID, concealed carry license, or government public assistance ID. Without ID you get a provisional ballot that counts only if you show ID before the county canvass.

KY.registrationDeadlineNote: Online registration must be received by 4:00 p.m. local time on October 5, 2026. Mailed registrations postmarked October 5, 2026 count.
KY.earlyVotingNote: No-excuse in-person early voting is October 29, 30, and 31, 2026. Excused in-person absentee voting (you must have a listed reason) is October 21, 22, 23, 26, 27, and 28, 2026.
KY.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. Reasons include age, disability, or illness; being absent from the county during all in-person voting days; students temporarily outside the county; temporary residence outside the state; military and overseas voters; jailed but not convicted; and address confidentiality program participants.
KY.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the county clerk before 6:00 p.m.
KY.idRequirement: You must show ID at the polls. A photo ID with your name, such as a driver license, military ID, college ID, or Kentucky government ID, is standard. If you cannot get a photo ID, you may sign a Reasonable Impediment Declaration and show a non-photo ID such as a Social Security card or credit or debit card, or an election officer who knows you may sign an affirmation.

LA.registrationDeadlineNote: October 5, 2026 is the deadline to register in person or by mail. Online registration through the Secretary of State site is open until October 13, 2026.
LA.earlyVotingNote: Any voter may vote early at the parish registrar of voters office, no reason needed. Offices are open 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. each day of early voting.
LA.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. Reasons include age 65 or older, being temporarily out of the parish or state, students and staff living outside the parish, hospitalization, physical disability, incarceration without a felony conviction, and a few others. Military and overseas voters need no excuse.
LA.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 2, 2026, received by the parish registrar by 4:30 p.m. (military, overseas and hospitalized voters: 8 p.m. on November 3, 2026)
LA.idRequirement: You will be asked for a photo ID such as a Louisiana driver's license, Louisiana special ID, LA Wallet digital license, or another recognized picture ID with your name and signature. If you have no photo ID you may sign a voter affidavit and still vote.

ME.registrationDeadlineNote: Mail and online registration must be received by the 21st day before Election Day, computed as October 13, 2026 from the stated rule. You can also register in person at your town office or at the polls through Election Day.
ME.earlyVotingNote: Maine early voting is in-person absentee voting at your town or city clerk's office. Ballots become available 30 days before Election Day (October 4, 2026, computed from the stated rule) and the no-excuse period runs through Thursday, October 29, 2026.
ME.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
ME.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by your municipal clerk by 8 p.m.
ME.idRequirement: The state voter guide lists identification only for registering to vote (for example a driver's license, or a document showing your name and address). It does not describe an ID requirement for casting a ballot.

MD.registrationDeadlineNote: Regular registration closes the 21st day before the election. Mailed applications postmarked by that date are accepted. You can also register in person at an early voting center or your Election Day polling place with proof of where you live.
MD.earlyVotingNote: Early voting centers are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. every day, including Saturday and Sunday.
MD.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
MD.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received by 10 a.m. on November 13, 2026 (drop box or in person by 8 p.m. on November 3, 2026)
MD.idRequirement: Most voters do not need to show ID. Some first-time voters will be asked for ID: a current photo ID (Maryland driver's license, MVA ID, student, employee or military ID, U.S. passport, or other government-issued ID) or a current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck or government document with your name and address.

MA.registrationDeadlineNote: Register online, by mail or in person by October 24, 2026.
MA.earlyVotingNote: No excuse needed. Vote at any early voting site in your city or town. Local schedules and locations are posted by October 9, 2026.
MA.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
MA.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received by November 6, 2026 (drop box or in person by close of polls on November 3, 2026)
MA.idRequirement: Most voters are not asked for ID. You may be asked to show ID if you are voting for the first time in Massachusetts, are on the inactive voter list, are casting a provisional or challenged ballot, or a poll worker has a legal reason to ask. Any ID with your name and registered address works, such as a driver's license, state ID, utility bill, lease or rent receipt.

MI.registrationDeadlineNote: October 19, 2026 is the last day to register by mail or online. From October 20 through 8 p.m. on Election Day you can register in person at your city or township clerk's office with proof of residency.
MI.earlyVotingNote: Nine days of early in-person voting are required statewide; some communities offer more days. Absentee ballots can also be voted in person at the clerk's office once available.
MI.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
MI.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by your clerk by 8 p.m.
MI.idRequirement: Bring a photo ID if you have one. A photo ID is not required to vote: voters without one can sign an affidavit and still cast a regular ballot.

MN.registrationDeadlineNote: October 13, 2026 is the pre-registration deadline. You can also register at your polling place on Election Day, or when voting early in person, with proof of residence.
MN.earlyVotingNote: In-person absentee voting at your county or city election office starts September 18, 2026. From October 16 through November 2, 2026 you can vote early in person and put your ballot directly in a ballot counter.
MN.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any eligible voter can apply for a ballot by mail. You do not need to be registered to apply.
MN.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by your election office by Election Day
MN.idRequirement: Voters who are already registered generally do not need to show ID; depending on when you registered you may need to bring proof of residence. To register at the polls you need proof of residence, such as an ID with your current name and address, or a photo ID plus a document with your current name and address.

MS.registrationDeadlineNote: Register in person at the Circuit or Municipal Clerk's office, or have your mailed application postmarked, by October 5, 2026.
MS.earlyVotingNote: Mississippi has no no-excuse early voting. Voters with a qualifying reason (for example age 65 or older, disability, away from the county on Election Day, or working during poll hours) can vote absentee in person at the Circuit Clerk's office within 45 days of the election until noon on Saturday, October 31, 2026. The state calendar lists September 21, 2026 as the earliest day; the state absentee page says beginning September 19, 2026, which is a Saturday. Clerks' offices are also open 8 a.m. to noon on October 24 and October 31, 2026.
MS.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. Mailed absentee ballots are limited to voters temporarily living outside their county, voters with a temporary or permanent disability, caregivers of hospitalized disabled persons, voters age 65 or older, and incarcerated voters not convicted of a disqualifying crime.
MS.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received by 5 p.m. on November 10, 2026
MS.idRequirement: Photo ID is required to vote in person, such as a Mississippi driver's license, U.S. passport, military ID, or any current photo ID issued by the U.S. or a state government. Without one you can cast an affidavit ballot and it will count if you show acceptable photo ID at the clerk's office within five business days after Election Day.

MO.registrationDeadlineNote: Registration forms must be postmarked or submitted by October 7, 2026 (the fourth Wednesday before the election).
MO.earlyVotingNote: Missouri offers no-excuse absentee voting in person from the second Tuesday before the election through the day before the election. Dates are computed from that stated rule. Locations are set by your local election authority. Photo ID is required.
MO.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required for a mailed ballot: absence from the jurisdiction on Election Day, illness or physical disability, religious belief or practice, work as an election worker, first responder, health care worker or law enforcement, incarceration while still eligible, or address confidentiality program participation. Most mailed ballots must be notarized.
MO.idRequirement: You must show a photo ID: a non-expired Missouri driver or non-driver license, a non-expired military or veteran ID, a non-expired U.S. passport, or another photo ID issued by the U.S. or Missouri. Without one you can cast a provisional ballot that counts if you return with photo ID that day or your signature matches your registration record.

MT.registrationDeadlineNote: Regular registration closes October 5, 2026 (mailed forms postmarked by that date and received within 3 days count). Late registration is available in person at the county election office from October 6 through noon on Election Day, November 3, 2026.
MT.earlyVotingNote: Montana has no separate early voting; you can vote an absentee ballot in person at your county election office. Ballots must be available for in-person voting by October 5, 2026. Applications for a one-time absentee ballot are due by noon on November 2, 2026.
MT.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
MT.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received at the election office or a polling place by 8 p.m.
MT.idRequirement: Election workers ask for photo ID at the polls, such as a Montana driver's license or state ID, military ID, tribal photo ID, U.S. passport, Montana concealed carry permit, or Montana University System photo ID. Without one of those you can show another photo ID plus a current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck or government document with your name and address. If you have no ID, ask your county election official about provisional voting.

NE.registrationDeadlineNote: In-person registration closes at 6 PM on October 23, 2026. Mail registrations must be postmarked, and online registrations completed, by October 16, 2026.
NE.earlyVotingNote: Early voting in person is at the county clerk or election commissioner office.
NE.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
NE.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by 8:00 PM Central Time (7:00 PM Mountain Time)
NE.idRequirement: Voters must show an acceptable photo ID such as a Nebraska driver's license or state ID, Nebraska college ID, U.S. passport, military ID, or tribal ID. The ID may be expired. Voters without an ID may sign a reasonable impediment certification or vote a provisional ballot. Mail ballot applicants must write their driver's license or state ID number on the application or enclose a copy of an acceptable ID.

NH.registrationDeadlineNote: The official page says you can register at your town or city clerk's office up to 6 to 13 days before the election, and at the supervisors of the checklist session held 6 to 13 days before each state election. The exact cutoff date varies by town, so no single statewide date is printed. You can also register at the polls on Election Day.
NH.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Only voters with an excuse: out of town on Election Day, religious observance, physical disability or illness, an employment or caregiving commitment during the entire time polls are open, confinement in a penal institution for a misdemeanor or awaiting trial, membership in the Address Confidentiality Program or protection by a domestic violence order, or a National Weather Service winter storm, blizzard, or ice storm warning for your town on Election Day.
NH.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by 5:00 p.m. on Election Day if returned by mail; if returned in person to the clerk, by 5:00 p.m. on November 2, 2026, the day before the election

NJ.registrationDeadlineNote: Registration closes 21 days before the election.
NJ.earlyVotingNote: Early voting sites are open at least 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Sunday.
NJ.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any active registered voter, no excuse needed.
NJ.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received by November 9, 2026
NJ.idRequirement: Most voters are not asked for ID at the polls. You may be asked to show ID only if you registered by mail in your county after January 1, 2003 and never voted in a federal election, or if you did not provide a driver's license number or last four Social Security digits when registering, or those numbers could not be verified. Any valid current photo ID, or a current document with your name and address such as a bank statement or utility bill, is accepted; without it you vote a provisional paper ballot.

NM.registrationDeadlineNote: Regular registration closes 28 days before the election; this date is computed from that stated rule. Same day registration is available after that at county clerk offices, early voting sites, and on Election Day.
NM.earlyVotingNote: Early voting starts at the county clerk's office 28 days before the election and ends the Saturday before the election; dates are computed from those stated rules. Expanded early voting sites open later, on the third Saturday before Election Day.
NM.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
NM.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day
NM.idRequirement: Most voters do not need to show a physical ID. Voters give a verbal or written statement of their name, year of birth, and registered address. First-time voters who registered by mail without ID, and voters registering the same day they vote, must show ID.

NY.registrationDeadlineNote: Applications must be received by the county board of elections by October 24, 2026.
NY.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter may apply for an early mail ballot, no excuse needed. Absentee ballots remain available for voters with a listed reason.
NY.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received by November 10, 2026; or delivered in person by 9 p.m. on November 3, 2026
NY.idRequirement: Most voters do not need to show ID at the polls. The Board of Elections checks your identity when you register using your DMV number or last four Social Security digits. If the Board could not verify your identity before Election Day, you will be asked for ID (such as a valid photo ID, utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document with your name and address) when voting for the first time.
NY.officialSiteLabel: New York State Board of Elections

NC.registrationDeadlineNote: Regular registration closes at 5 p.m. on October 9, 2026. Same-day registration is available at early voting sites during the early voting period.
NC.earlyVotingNote: Early voting ends at 3 p.m. on October 31, 2026.
NC.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
NC.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day
NC.idRequirement: Voters must show an acceptable photo ID when checking in to vote early or on Election Day. Voters without ID can vote a provisional ballot and fill out a Photo ID Exception Form. Mail voters must include a photocopy of an acceptable ID or complete an ID Exception Form.
NC.officialSiteLabel: North Carolina State Board of Elections

ND.registrationDeadlineNote: North Dakota does not have voter registration. You need a valid form of ID to vote.
ND.earlyVotingNote: Some counties offer early voting at certain dates and times before Election Day; dates vary by county. Absentee voting begins September 24, 2026.
ND.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any qualified elector may apply for an absentee ballot. The state absentee ballot application does not ask for a reason. You are never mailed a ballot without first requesting one.
ND.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by close of polls
ND.idRequirement: Voters must show a North Dakota driver's license or non-driver ID, a tribal ID or tribal letter, or a long-term care certificate showing a current address. Voters with an outdated address on a North Dakota ID may add a current bank statement, utility bill, paycheck, or government document. Voters without valid ID may cast a set-aside ballot and must show ID within 13 days after the election. Absentee applications also require valid ID information.

OK.registrationDeadlineNote: Registration applications must be received or postmarked by October 9, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 general election.
OK.earlyVotingNote: Early in-person absentee voting at county election board sites: October 28 to 30, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., and October 31, 8 a.m. to 2 p.m.
OK.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed. Standard absentee ballot affidavits must be notarized.
OK.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the County Election Board by 7:00 p.m.
OK.idRequirement: Voters show a photo ID issued by the U.S. government, State of Oklahoma, or a federally recognized tribal government, or the free voter identification card mailed by the county election board. Voters without ID may vote a provisional ballot after signing an affidavit.

OR.registrationDeadlineNote: Registration cards postmarked by October 13, 2026 or submitted online by 11:59 p.m. that day are valid.
OR.earlyVotingNote: Oregon votes by mail. There is no traditional early in-person voting. Ballots are mailed to active registered voters starting October 14, 2026, and can be returned by mail or to any official drop box.
OR.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Every active registered voter is mailed a ballot automatically. No request is needed.
OR.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received by November 10, 2026; ballots placed in a drop box must be received by 8 p.m. on November 3, 2026
OR.idRequirement: No ID is required to cast a mailed ballot. To register you provide an Oregon driver license, permit, or ID card number, or the last four digits of your Social Security number and a signature.

PA.registrationDeadlineNote: Last day to register before the November 3, 2026 general election.
PA.earlyVotingNote: Pennsylvania has no traditional early voting. Once county ballots are ready, a voter can go to the county election office, apply for a mail ballot, vote it, and return it in one visit, through the October 27, 2026 mail ballot application deadline.
PA.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter may apply for a mail-in ballot, no excuse needed. Absentee ballots are for voters who will be out of their municipality or have a disability or illness.
PA.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the county election office by 8:00 p.m.
PA.idRequirement: ID is required only the first time you vote at a polling place. Acceptable forms include a Pennsylvania driver's license or PennDOT ID, U.S. passport, government or military ID, student or employee ID, or a non-photo document such as a utility bill or voter registration confirmation with your name and address.

RI.registrationDeadlineNote: Registration must be made at least 30 days before the general election. The official calendar lists October 4, 2026.
RI.earlyVotingNote: Early in-person voting runs Wednesday, October 14 through Monday, November 2, 2026, ending at 4 p.m., at your city or town hall or a designated location during regular business hours.
RI.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed. Emergency mail ballots are available at local boards from October 14 through November 2, 2026 at 4 p.m.
RI.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the State Board of Elections by 8:00 p.m.
RI.idRequirement: A valid photo ID is required to vote in person, such as a Rhode Island driver's license, U.S. passport, tribal ID, student ID, military ID, government-issued ID, or Rhode Island Voter ID card, not expired more than 6 months before the election. Voters without an acceptable photo ID vote an emergency mail ballot at the polls.

SC.registrationDeadlineNote: Online, fax, or email registration by 11:59 p.m. October 4, 2026. In person by 5 p.m. October 2, 2026. Mail registration must be postmarked by October 5, 2026.
SC.earlyVotingNote: Early voting centers are open Monday through Saturday, 8:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., closed Sunday, October 25. All registered voters may vote early.
SC.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. Reasons include age 65 or older, physical disability, absence from the county, work obligations during early voting hours, caring for a sick or disabled person, confinement in jail, military or overseas status, and emergency hospitalization.
SC.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the county voter registration office by 7:00 p.m.
SC.idRequirement: Voters show a photo ID: SC driver's license, SC DMV ID card, SC voter registration card with photo, U.S. passport, or federal military ID. Voters with a reasonable impediment to getting a photo ID may sign an affidavit and cast a provisional ballot.

SD.registrationDeadlineNote: Register by 5:00 p.m. local time on October 19, 2026, fifteen days before the election.
SD.earlyVotingNote: South Dakota offers in-person absentee voting at the county auditor's office starting September 18, 2026 and running until 5 p.m. on November 2, 2026.
SD.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter may request an absentee ballot by submitting an application to the county auditor.
SD.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the county election official in time to deliver to the precinct before polls close
SD.idRequirement: Voters show a photo ID: South Dakota driver's license or nondriver ID, U.S. government photo ID such as a passport, U.S. Armed Forces ID, current South Dakota student photo ID, or tribal photo ID. Voters without photo ID may sign a personal identification affidavit and vote a regular ballot.

TN.registrationDeadlineNote: Voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 State and Federal General Election.
TN.earlyVotingNote: Early voting runs Wednesday, October 14 through Thursday, October 29, 2026.
TN.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. Reasons include age 60 or older, being outside the county during early voting and on Election Day, hospitalization or illness or disability, caring for someone who is ill or disabled, full-time student outside the county, nursing home residency, jury duty, religious observance, and being on the permanent absentee list.
TN.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the county election commission by the close of polls; must be returned by mail or delivery service, not by hand
TN.idRequirement: Voters must show a federal or Tennessee state photo ID with their name and photograph. Voters without ID may vote a provisional ballot and have two business days after Election Day to show a valid photo ID at the election commission office.

TX.registrationDeadlineNote: Last day to register to vote for the November 3, 2026 general election.
TX.earlyVotingNote: Early voting by personal appearance runs Monday, October 19 through Friday, October 30, 2026.
TX.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. You may vote by mail if you are 65 or older, sick or disabled, expected to give birth within three weeks of Election Day, away from your county during early voting and on Election Day, or confined in jail or civil commitment.
TX.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by 7:00 p.m., or if postmarked by 7:00 p.m. on November 3, received by 5:00 p.m. on November 4, 2026
TX.idRequirement: Voters show one of seven photo IDs: Texas driver license, election ID certificate, personal ID card, handgun license, U.S. military ID, U.S. citizenship certificate with photo, or U.S. passport. Voters who cannot reasonably obtain one may show a supporting document such as a utility bill or bank statement and sign a reasonable impediment declaration.

UT.registrationDeadlineNote: Register by 5:00 p.m. on October 23, 2026 to avoid voting a provisional ballot. After that you can still register in person at an early voting location or a vote center on Election Day with two forms of ID.
UT.earlyVotingNote: Early in-person voting dates are set by each county. The state calendar says early voting can begin up to 14 days before Election Day and must last at least four days. Check with your county clerk.
UT.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Utah votes mainly by mail. Every active registered voter is mailed a ballot automatically. Ballots start going out October 23, 2026.
UT.idRequirement: In person, show one valid photo ID with your name, or two forms of ID that together prove your name and current address. Voters registering at the polls need two acceptable IDs, one for identity and one for residence.

VT.registrationDeadlineNote: Vermont has no registration deadline. You may register any day up to and including Election Day, at your town clerk's office or at the polls.
VT.earlyVotingNote: Town clerks must have general election ballots by September 19, 2026 (45 days before the election), and voters may vote early at the clerk's office once ballots arrive. In-person early voting at the clerk's office ends at close of business November 2, 2026.
VT.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Every active registered voter is automatically mailed a general election ballot, with mailing completed by October 1, 2026. Any voter can also request an early or absentee ballot from the town clerk.
VT.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the town clerk or polling place by 7:00 p.m.
VT.idRequirement: No ID is required to vote in person. First-time registrants who register by mail or online must include a copy of an acceptable ID such as a driver's license, passport, utility bill, bank statement, or other government document.

VA.registrationDeadlineNote: Regular registration closes October 23, 2026. After that, you can still register in person and vote a provisional ballot through Election Day.
VA.earlyVotingNote: Early in-person voting runs at your general registrar's office through 5:00 p.m. October 31, 2026. Some offices also open on the last two Saturdays and Sundays.
VA.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
VA.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received by noon on November 6, 2026 (or returned in person by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day)
VA.idRequirement: Show an acceptable ID (photo or non-photo, including an expired DMV license) or sign an ID Confirmation Statement to vote a regular ballot. Voters who decline both may vote a provisional ballot.

WA.registrationDeadlineNote: Online and mail registrations must be received by October 26, 2026 (8 days before Election Day). You can register or update in person at your county elections office through 8:00 p.m. on November 3, 2026.
WA.earlyVotingNote: Washington votes by mail. Ballots are mailed October 16, 2026, and county voting centers with accessible voting units are open through 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
WA.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Every registered voter is mailed a ballot automatically. No request is needed.
WA.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026 if mailed, or placed in an official drop box by 8:00 p.m. on November 3, 2026
WA.idRequirement: No ID is shown to vote by mail. You sign the ballot return envelope and the county compares your signature to your registration record.

WV.registrationDeadlineNote: Registration closes 21 days before the election. No same-day registration.
WV.earlyVotingNote: Early voting runs at the county courthouse or designated locations during business hours, plus 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on the last two Saturdays before the election.
WV.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Excuse required. Includes voters with a disability or illness, voters who will be out of the county, military and overseas voters, students, incarcerated voters not convicted of a felony, and other reasons listed on the application.
WV.mailBallotReturnDeadline: Postmarked by November 3, 2026, received before the canvass begins on November 9, 2026. Ballots without a postmark count if received by November 4, 2026.
WV.idRequirement: Show a photo ID such as a driver's license, state ID, passport, military ID, government employee ID, or WV student ID. Voters without ID may vote if a poll worker has known them for six months, or with a signed sworn statement from an adult with valid ID who has known them six months, or vote a provisional ballot. ID does not apply to absentee by mail voters.

WI.registrationDeadlineNote: Online and mail registration closes 20 days before the election. This date is computed from the stated rule. You can register in person at your municipal clerk's office through October 30, 2026 (the Friday before), and at the polls on Election Day. Proof of residence is required.
WI.earlyVotingNote: In-person absentee voting may begin no earlier than 14 days before the election (Wisconsin Statute 6.86(1)(b)); October 20, 2026 is computed from that stated rule. Hours and locations are set by each municipal clerk, and the last possible day is Sunday, November 1, 2026. Check with your clerk for the actual start date and hours.
WI.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed. A copy of your photo ID is required with the request.
WI.idRequirement: Most voters must show an acceptable photo ID, such as a Wisconsin driver license or state ID, passport, military ID, tribal ID, or a compliant student ID. Free state ID cards are available from the DMV.

WY.registrationDeadlineNote: Mail registration must be received by October 19, 2026. After that you can still register in person at the county clerk and vote absentee October 20 through November 2, 2026, or register at your polling place on Election Day.
WY.earlyVotingNote: In-person absentee voting at the county clerk's office runs October 6 through November 2, 2026.
WY.mailBallotWhoCanRequest: Any registered voter, no excuse needed.
WY.mailBallotReturnDeadline: November 3, 2026, received by the county clerk by 7:00 p.m.
WY.idRequirement: Show an acceptable ID such as a Wyoming or other state driver's license or ID card, tribal ID, U.S. passport, military ID, Wyoming student photo ID, Medicare or Medicaid card, or Wyoming concealed carry permit.
